name: fluentcart-mcp
description: Curated and capability-discovered tools for a FluentCart store — orders, products, customers, subscriptions, coupons and reports. Read-only unless you opt in to writes.
long_description:
Connects an MCP client to the FluentCart REST API of your own WordPress site.

Dynamic mode is the default: a handful of meta-tools let the agent search the catalogue, read a tool definition and execute it, which keeps the definition payload small no matter how large the store API grows. Curated mode advertises a small reviewed set directly, code mode exposes a sandboxed scripting pair, and full mode lists everything the current policy permits.

Exposure is decided before anything is listed. Writes are hidden entirely until write mode is raised, and what you actually get depends on what your store and your role support. FluentCart native abilities are a separate read-only opt-in with their own credentials; discovery admits only the audited read allowlist.

store_url.title: WordPress URL
store_url.description: Full URL of the WordPress site running FluentCart (e.g. https://your-store.com).

username.title: WordPress Username
username.description: WordPress user whose role grants the FluentCart REST capabilities you need.

app_password.title: Application Password
app_password.description: Generate at WordPress Admin > Users > Profile > Application Passwords.

write_mode.title: Write Mode
write_mode.description: disabled (read-only, the default) or reversible (writes with a verified undo).

abilities_mode.title: Native Abilities Bridge
abilities_mode.description: disabled (default) or enabled. Adds only audited FluentCart native read abilities after live discovery.

abilities_username.title: Abilities Username
abilities_username.description: Separate WordPress user for the optional read-only Abilities bridge. Required when the bridge is enabled.

abilities_app_password.title: Abilities Application Password
abilities_app_password.description: Separate WordPress Application Password for the optional read-only Abilities bridge.

tools.name: fluentcart_app_init
tools.description: Get app bootstrap data: shop config, REST config, asset URLs. Translation strings excluded.

tools.name: fluentcart_coupon_create
tools.description: Create a new coupon. For fixed type, amount is in cents. For percentage, amount is the percent value (e.g. 15 = 15% off).

tools.name: fluentcart_coupon_get
tools.description: Get one coupon: use_count, start and end dates, and the conditions object that decides eligibility — included_products, included_categories, max_uses, min_purchase_amount. An unknown coupon id answers HTTP 200 with coupon:null rather than an error, so a null coupon means no such coupon, never a coupon without details.

tools.name: fluentcart_coupon_list
tools.description: List coupons with optional search. Rows carry use_count against the max_uses cap, plus start_date and end_date, so expiry and redemption limits are answerable without fetching every coupon. status is derived rather than merely stored: a coupon past its end_date reads expired. Statuses: active, inactive, expired, scheduled. Types: percentage, fixed, free_shipping. amount is a percent for percentage, minor units for fixed.

tools.name: fluentcart_coupon_update
tools.description: Update a coupon using fetch-merge pattern. Fetches current state, merges your changes, submits full payload. Types: percentage, fixed, free_shipping.

tools.name: fluentcart_customer_get
tools.description: One customer in full, including the figures a stats question is usually after: purchase_count, ltv (lifetime value) and aov (average order value) in CENTS summed across currencies, first_purchase_date and last_purchase_date, plus labels and address count.

tools.name: fluentcart_customer_list
tools.description: Find customers by name or email, or list them sorted. Each row carries ltv (lifetime value), aov (average order value), purchase_count and the first and last purchase dates. ltv and aov are CENTS, summed across every currency the customer paid in, so sort by ltv DESC for top spenders. Numbers arrive as strings.

tools.name: fluentcart_dashboard_overview
tools.description: Store dashboard tiles for the LAST 30 DAYS — product count, order count, revenue and refund totals. The window is fixed and takes no arguments, so these are not all-time figures. For a period you choose, use fluentcart_report_sales_summary. Values in cents.

tools.name: fluentcart_describe_tools
tools.description: Get the full input schema, annotations and risk classification for specific tools by name. Use after searching, to learn exact parameters before executing. Maximum 5 tools per call.

tools.name: fluentcart_execute_code
tools.description: Run JavaScript in an isolated WebAssembly sandbox to compose several FluentCart reads into one answer, avoiding a round trip per call. Write plain JavaScript (ES2023) and `return` one JSON-serialisable value. Call reads with `await fluentcart.call(operation, input)`. There is no network, filesystem, environment, timer, module system or console. At most 10 calls, 5 seconds and 24000 characters of output per execution. The sandbox cannot write, refund, delete or reach anything except the read operations returned by fluentcart_search_api.

tools.name: fluentcart_execute_read_tool
tools.description: Execute a read-only FluentCart tool by name. Refuses any tool that changes state; use the matching write executor for those.

tools.name: fluentcart_execute_reversible_write
tools.description: Execute a FluentCart write that has a verified read-back and a supported delete or restore. Requires FLUENTCART_WRITE_MODE=reversible. Refuses destructive and real-money actions.

tools.name: fluentcart_order_get
tools.description: Full order details for one order: the lines bought, the transactions against it, the customer, and the billing and shipping address it is to be delivered to. This is the tool that answers where to ship an order — the address is already on the order, and no other read carries it.

tools.name: fluentcart_order_list
tools.description: List orders with customer names. Filter by date range, status tab, or search. Search matches customer name, email, and invoice number. There is NO customer filter: a customer_id parameter is silently ignored and you get every order in the store back. To get one customer's orders, either search by their email, or use fluentcart_order_customer_orders, which takes a customer id properly. Tabs: paid, completed, processing, refunded, subscription, renewal.

tools.name: fluentcart_order_transactions
tools.description: Get all transactions for an order. Types: charge, refund. Statuses: succeeded, pending, failed, refunded, disputed.

tools.name: fluentcart_product_get
tools.description: Get one product with its variants, detail, media and metadata. Prices on each variant are in minor units (cents).

tools.name: fluentcart_product_list
tools.description: List products with optional filtering by type, status, fulfilment, and search. Its search covers variant names as well as product titles, so a colour or size a customer named finds the product it belongs to — nothing else in the registry does that. Use active_view to filter by product type or status. Includes drafts.

tools.name: fluentcart_product_search_by_name
tools.description: Find products by name, returning id, title, price range, stock and fulfilment type — enough to pick one and then fetch it with fluentcart_product_get. Pass category_id to list a category instead; this is the only way to see which products are filed under a term. Matches PRODUCT TITLES ONLY — a colour or size that exists solely as a variant name finds nothing here, so use fluentcart_product_list for those. Published products only, ten to a page, so read has_more before believing a total. Omitting every argument returns the first page of the catalogue rather than nothing.

tools.name: fluentcart_report_sales_summary
tools.description: Store sales, refunds and order totals for one currency over an inclusive date range: gross_sales, net_revenue, tax, shipping, refunded_amount, refunded_orders, order_count and average_order_value — so it also gives a refund rate: refunded_orders over order_count. Counts orders with payment status paid, refunded, partially_paid or partially_refunded, test-mode included — FluentCart applies no mode filter. Counts, money totals, date filtering and currency scoping are reconciled against the order list by a live test; day boundaries in the store timezone remain approximate. Every result states its period, scope and currency, and carries its own warnings. Refunds are attributed to the order's creation date, so a closed period can still move when an old order is refunded.

tools.name: fluentcart_report_sales_trend
tools.description: Sales, net revenue and order count bucketed over time for one currency. Every bucket in range is returned, empty ones included. FluentCart widens the bucket on long ranges — daily to 91 days, monthly to a year, yearly beyond — so the result reports the granularity requested and the one actually applied, and warns when they differ. Counts orders with payment status paid, refunded, partially_paid or partially_refunded, test-mode included — FluentCart applies no mode filter. Counts, money totals, date filtering and currency scoping are reconciled against the order list by a live test; day boundaries in the store timezone remain approximate. Every result states its period, scope and currency, and carries its own warnings.

tools.name: fluentcart_report_top_products
tools.description: The 20 best-selling products over an inclusive date range, ranked by units sold rather than revenue. Counts orders with payment status paid, refunded, partially_paid or partially_refunded, test-mode included — FluentCart applies no mode filter. Counts, money totals, date filtering and currency scoping are reconciled against the order list by a live test; day boundaries in the store timezone remain approximate. Every result states its period, scope and currency, and carries its own warnings. Product names come from the most recent matching order line, so a renamed product appears under the title it last sold as.

tools.name: fluentcart_search_api
tools.description: Find read-only FluentCart operations by keyword. Returns up to 5 compact TypeScript declarations you can call from fluentcart_execute_code. Only operations that read data are ever returned; writes, refunds and deletions are not available in code mode.

tools.name: fluentcart_search_tools
tools.description: Search available FluentCart tools by keyword and optional category. Returns one compact line per match including its risk class and how it executes. Use this to discover tools before describing or executing them.

tools.name: fluentcart_subscription_get
tools.description: Get subscription details including billing dates, gateway info, and payment history. Amounts in cents.

tools.name: fluentcart_subscription_list
tools.description: List subscriptions with optional filtering. Money fields — recurring_amount, recurring_total, signup_fee — are MINOR UNITS: 99900 with currency EUR is 999.00 EUR, not 99,900. Reading them as decimals overstates a plan by two orders of magnitude. Statuses: active, trialing, paused, intended, failing, past_due, expiring, canceled, expired, completed. Only nine of those are filterable with active_view; for past_due or completed pass the status as search, which matches the status column.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Modern HTTP requests work without MCP session state.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The v2 Streamable HTTP transport accepts independent discovery and tool requests.

proofs.assertion: Raw modern HTTP requests complete without an MCP-Session-Id request or response header.

protocolCompliance.requirement: The server exposes the 2026-07-28 discovery operation.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The official v2 SDK serves server discovery for the modern protocol.

proofs.assertion: Raw HTTP and STDIO discovery responses report the selected protocol and supported versions.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Subscription capabilities are declared only when implemented.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The server provides request-response tools and does not expose subscription capabilities.

proofs.assertion: The server capability surface omits resource, prompt and tool-list subscriptions.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Methods removed from the modern protocol are not exposed.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The modern surface contains discovery and tool operations, not removed legacy methods.

proofs.assertion: The raw modern contract rejects or omits methods outside the declared surface.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Task capabilities are declared only when implemented.
protocolCompliance.rationale: Long-running MCP tasks are outside this synchronous FluentCart tool server.

proofs.assertion: Discovery and capabilities contain no tasks extension.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Multi-round-trip responses are declared only when implemented.
protocolCompliance.rationale: Every exposed operation completes as a single request-response exchange.

proofs.assertion: The advertised modern surface contains no multi-round-trip response capability.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Modern discovery and tool results carry SDK-defined result type metadata.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The v2 SDK emits standard result-type metadata for modern responses.

proofs.assertion: Discovery, list and tool response metadata is asserted on the raw wire.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Stream resumability is declared only when implemented.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The server intentionally has no SSE stream, event store or resumption token.

proofs.assertion: HTTP GET does not open an SSE stream and the transport creates no resumable session.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Protocol extensions are declared only when implemented.
protocolCompliance.rationale: No custom protocol extension namespace is exposed.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Trace-context propagation is declared only when implemented.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The server emits structured operational logs but does not advertise trace propagation.

proofs.assertion: Logging remains an internal stderr concern and is not exposed as an MCP capability.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Repeated list operations return a deterministic order.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The server owns and tests the stable order of its exposed tool registry.

proofs.assertion: Repeated raw tools/list calls return the same ordered names.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Modern HTTP responses use the protocol standard headers.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The official v2 HTTP transport supplies the selected protocol and metadata headers.

proofs.assertion: Raw responses assert the modern protocol and content-type header contract.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Cacheable operations expose explicit cache metadata.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The server defines private zero-TTL hints for every cache-aware operation.

proofs.assertion: The six cache-aware operation families return exact private zero-TTL hints.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Resource and request failures use modern structured JSON-RPC errors.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The v2 SDK maps invalid input and server policy failures to structured error responses.

proofs.assertion: Raw requests assert -32602, -32020 and -32022 error allocations.

protocolCompliance.requirement: OAuth issuer and dynamic client registration requirements are applied when relevant.
protocolCompliance.rationale: This private server authenticates with a static Bearer token and is neither an OAuth client nor an authorisation server.

proofs.assertion: Private HTTP authentication is a configured Bearer token boundary with no OAuth endpoints.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Tool schemas use the SDK modern JSON Schema dialect contract.
protocolCompliance.rationale: Tool schemas are registered and serialised by the official v2 SDK.

proofs.assertion: The SDK v2 registration and generated schema contract is pinned by executable tests.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Protocol and application errors occupy their allocated JSON-RPC ranges.
protocolCompliance.rationale: Protocol validation and server policy failures use distinct standard and server ranges.

proofs.assertion: Raw negative cases assert the exact standard and server error codes.

protocolCompliance.requirement: Deprecated transports and optional capability aliases are absent.
protocolCompliance.rationale: The server exposes STDIO and stateless Streamable HTTP without Roots, Sampling, MCP Logging, resumability or legacy HTTP+SSE.

proofs.assertion: The raw modern surface omits Roots, Sampling, MCP Logging and deprecated HTTP+SSE.
